title: Asymmetric route mapping causes cross-tenant flow duplication and intermittent egress failures
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: Several Dedicated customers reported sporadic cross-tenant traffic observations and intermittent egress failures during peak windows. Investigation shows an asymmetric route mapping bug in the per-tenant overlay reconciliation code that can duplicate outbound flows onto a stale interface mapping. This manifests as duplicated connections, occasional TCP RSTs, and intermittent DNS resolution failures for affected tenants. Impact: customer-facing errors (timeouts, retried requests), increased egress costs, and potential data plane confusion across up to 3% of active sessions during high churn events. Systems involved: tenant route reconciler, overlay translation table (ORT), NAT/conntrack namespaces, BGP peering sync, kube-proxy egress rules, and our DNS caching layer for Dedicated clusters.
reproduction_steps: 1) Create two tenants sharing a peering target and trigger rapid scale-up/scale-down of host pods (~1000 events/min).
2) Force overlay reconciliation by toggling tenant autoscaler policy or applying a redeploy.
3) Observe duplicated outbound SYN packets on the node-level tcpdump: same source/port but different underlay interface mapping.
4) Verify connection resets reported by app servers and intermittent DNS NXDOMAINs due to queries sent over mismatched resolver paths.
timeline_of_work: 2026-02-18: PagerDuty sig: initial alert from customer A (latency spikes + TCP RSTs). Started incident call.
2026-02-18: Identified spike correlated with overlay reconciliation churn (reconciler logs showing rapid mapping flips).
2026-02-19: Reproduced in staging with synthetic churn. Confirmed ORT entries were being written twice under rare race.
2026-02-20: Emergency hotfix deployed to Dedicated staging: guard added to ORT writer to serialize updates. Reduced duplication but not full fix.
2026-02-21: Rollout to a small subset of production clusters for mitigation. Customer-facing errors decreased by ~70%.
2026-02-25: Root cause analysis completed: race between route-reconciler’s delta-calculation and the peer-gc job causing stale mapping resurrection.
2026-03-02: Implemented transactional update for ORT + extended reconciliation backoff. Added canary tests and e2e network churn test.
2026-03-04: Internal security review requested due to cross-tenant observation; added audit logging for ORT mutations.
2026-03-05: Change submitted for review (PR #1482). Preparing release notes and customer comms.
decision_log: Trade-off: Synchronous ORT writes add ~2-4ms per reconciliation loop but prevents duplication and cross-tenant exposure. Chosen to accept latency increase for safety (P0 customer impact).
Alternative considered: aggressive GC of stale mappings every 30s. Rejected because GC window caused transient unreachable periods for healthy tenants.
Added audit trail for all ORT writes to support post-incident compliance reviews.
implementation_notes: - Fix: make ORT updates transactional with compare-and-swap using revision numbers persisted in etcd. - Add per-tenant write locks keyed by tenant-id to prevent parallel reconciles. - Extend peer-gc backoff to avoid resurrecting mappings during active reconcilation. - Ensure conntrack namespace creation is idempotent and conflict-safe. - Add unit tests for ORT race scenarios and a new e2e test that simulates heavy scale churn.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Transactional writes increase reconciliation latency and could affect autoscaler responsiveness. Mitigation: measure latency in canary and add adaptive batching if >10ms p95.
Risk: Backporting fix to older dedicated clusters with custom kernel modules may require additional testing. Mitigation: prepare compatibility shim and staged rollout plan.
qa_and_rollout_plan: 1) Merge PRs and run CI + new e2e churn test. 2) Canary to 3 low-traffic clusters for 48 hours. Monitor tcpdump dedup rate, conntrack collisions, and customer error rates. 3) Roll to production clusters in waves of 10% with 2-hour verification windows. 4) Post-rollout: monitor for 7 days and schedule a postmortem review with affected customers.
customer_communications: 2026-02-19: Initial notice to affected customers acknowledging investigation and mitigation steps.
2026-03-05: Draft of technical incident summary and remediation timeline prepared for customer success review.
Planned: follow-up executive summary and credit offer for customers with sustained impact.
